capturedFrom: the original T-SQL object, deployed unchanged to a scratch SQL Server database with the fixed case's rows
review: Captured from the source engine, not derived independently. A reviewer checks each case's expected values against its label at step 5 (second review). Values are canonical: n: number, s: text, b: bit, d: date, t: timestamp (microseconds), x: bytes (hex), ∅: NULL.

cases.label: [A01] SearchDetails: Cyrillic values differing only in case match a case-insensitive search ('дом' finds 'ДОМ' and 'Дом', not 'дым' or 'ÉCLAIR')
[A02] SearchDetails: two matching rows share the same SearchDetails value (a non-key tie); both are returned in name order
[A03] SearchDetails: a search text ending in a space ('amy ') matches only values with a space after 'amy'
[A04] SearchDetails: a reversed range '[c-a]' (T-SQL accepts it; a regular expression rejects it as an invalid range)
[A05] SearchDetails: a search text ending in a backslash ('a\') is an ordinary character in T-SQL LIKE
[A06] SearchDetails: TOP(@MaximumRowsToReturn) returns exactly two of five hits, ordered by the Windows collation
[A07] SearchDetails: no row qualifies, so FOR JSON ... ROOT returns an empty string, not an empty array
[A08] SearchDetails: '_' matches a digit, an accented letter and a space ('x_9')
[A09] SearchDetails: the range class '[a-c]' matches single letters a, b and c, not the text '[a-c]'
[A10] SearchDetails: the class '[%_]' matches a literal percent or underscore, not the text '[%_]'
